correctness.rationale: For a resting core vertex an excited core, if any, is automatically a different vertex. Therefore each occupied initial pair type can retain one fixed tag, with equality of tagged states exactly equivalent to equality of the assigned labelled state at two times. An independent shared-signal-history enumeration checked all 65,535 nonempty supports, every supplied coefficient, least periods 1 or 4, all fifteen classes on supports of size at most four, and the unique all-rest fixed point. The support {(0,0),(0,1),(2,0)} first enters the fixed point at seven and extends to every admissible n by duplicating an initial tag, so F^10 differs from F^6 while F^11=F^7. For each coefficient the multiplicative count is the number of surjections from n labels onto the occupied tags. The support test also checked that cycling is equivalent to starting with all four core colors, and that every recurrent leaf has phase c-1. Such core colorings rotate without regard to leaves; four core phases and 4^n free initial leaf colorings give 4^(n+1) per orbit. Independent direct adjacency enumeration at n=4 agreed class by class (6,144 oscillatory states). Replay: python3 /workspace/repro/record2.py, output /workspace/repro/record2.out. This is an all-size reduction with a finite exhaustive certificate, not extrapolation from n=4. The frozen C++ checker was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: Adding one private leaf at each clique vertex is a natural perturbation that changes how long waves and extinction transients persist. Resolving the sharp entry bound, all labelled temporal populations and each orbit's basin for every size gives a usable benchmark beyond the eventual-period set. The finite support calculation is independent of clique size and the resulting population law can be used without enumerating labelled states.
